ambiguities.description: Tax ID is stated to not be a reliable unique identifier due to duplicate/parent-subsidiary entities, but is Tax ID mandatory for every vendor (e.g. is it required to reach active status, distinct from the risk review gate)? The relationship of tax documentation to status transition is unclear after the March rule change discussion.

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.
Tax form on file. Once the W-9 is in, they're live and a buyer can raise a PO. ... A vendor cannot be moved to active until a risk review has been completed and signed off.

ambiguities.description: The vendor record mentions three addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal), described as 'frequently different and frequently wrong,' but no data type, uniqueness, or mandatory rules were established for these; they were not modeled as fact types pending clarification of structure (single text field vs. structured address).

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: The term 'tier' is overloaded -- Dana's spend tier and Raj's risk tier are both called 'tier' informally causing confusion; while modeled as separate fields (SpendTier, RiskTier), the transcript notes ongoing terminology conflict that stakeholders have failed to resolve organizationally. Confirm final naming convention for documentation/UI to avoid ambiguity.

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." ... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: The post-suspension handling of in-flight purchase orders (a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and pending a steering group/Legal decision. No constraint should be modeled until this is settled; flagged here as an open policy gap rather than a captured rule.

source_references.excerpt: Then we need a middle state. Something like run-off -- existing POs complete, no new ones can be raised. ... This goes to the sourcing steering group.

ambiguities.description: Mei's personal spreadsheet contains a 'preferred vendor' flag used informally to choose between vendors supplying the same thing, but the criteria are acknowledged as ad hoc with no defined process; explicitly excluded from the model per stakeholder instruction, but flagged here since it represents a real business behavior not captured in the system.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Whether a Contact requires mandatory participation in the Vendor-Region-Contact fact type is unclear: contacts exist only for regions where a vendor operates, but it's not explicit whether every vendor-region combination that exists (i.e., where the vendor operates) must always have a contact populated immediately, or if there can be a gap before a contact is assigned.

source_references.excerpt: And can a vendor have no contact in a region? If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether 'Vendor operates in Region' should be modeled as its own fact type distinct from 'Vendor has primary Contact in Region' -- currently the operating relationship is only implied through the contact fact type, since a vendor 'operating' in a region without yet having assigned a contact seems structurally impossible per the transcript, but this may need separate representation for reporting.

source_references.excerpt: Since we went to regional sourcing last year, it's one primary contact per region. So a vendor operating in EMEA and APAC has two primary contacts, one for each region.

Confirm whether contacts are identified by a system-generated ID or simply by the vendor+region+name combination.
